# Where the widget goes, by framework

The rule everywhere: one copy per page, in the layout the pages share, running in the browser only, with the project's publishable key (an environment variable is fine; the key is public).

The code shows `https://support.opem.app` and `pk_…`. Use the host and key from `get_install_snippet` or from the snippet the developer pasted; the script tag below is the same string `get_install_snippet` returns and the dashboard's Install tab shows, which also has a "Your framework" picker with this code and the project's real key.

## JavaScript frameworks

### Next.js, app router

File: `app/layout.tsx`. The root layout, inside `<body>` after `{children}`, with `Script` from `next/script`.

```tsx
import Script from "next/script";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        {children}
        <Script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" strategy="afterInteractive" />
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

- Or wrap `{children}` in `OpemProvider` from `@opem/react` in a client component; the provider adds the script tag itself, so do not add both.
- `data-project` can read `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_OPEM_KEY` instead; the key is public, so a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable is fine.

Signing identities on the server: the Node.js sample in the `identify` skill's signing reference (`apps/web/snippets/identify-server.ts`).

### Next.js, pages router

File: `pages/_app.tsx`. The custom App, after `<Component {...pageProps} />`, with `Script` from `next/script`.

```tsx
import type { AppProps } from "next/app";
import Script from "next/script";

export default function App({ Component, pageProps }: AppProps) {
  return (
    <>
      <Component {...pageProps} />
      <Script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" strategy="afterInteractive" />
    </>
  );
}
```

- Or wrap `<Component {...pageProps} />` in `OpemProvider` from `@opem/react`; the provider adds the script tag itself, so do not add both.

Signing identities on the server: the Node.js sample in the `identify` skill's signing reference (`apps/web/snippets/identify-server.ts`).

### Remix

File: `app/root.tsx`. The root `Layout`, inside `<body>` after `<Scripts />`.

```tsx
import { Links, Meta, Scripts, ScrollRestoration } from "@remix-run/react";

export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <Meta />
        <Links />
      </head>
      <body>
        {children}
        <ScrollRestoration />
        <Scripts />
        <script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" defer></script>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

- On React Router 7 the same components come from `react-router`.
- Or wrap `<Outlet />` in `OpemProvider` from `@opem/react`; the provider adds the script tag itself, so do not add both.

Signing identities on the server: the Node.js sample in the `identify` skill's signing reference (`apps/web/snippets/identify-server.ts`).

### SvelteKit

File: `src/app.html`. The page template, before `</body>`, after the `%sveltekit.body%` element.

```html
<script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" defer></script>
```

- To read the key from `$env/static/public` instead, call `Opem.init({ projectKey: PUBLIC_OPEM_KEY })` from `@opem/browser` inside `onMount` in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`; `onMount` keeps it out of server rendering. Use one or the other, not both.

Signing identities on the server: the Node.js sample in the `identify` skill's signing reference (`apps/web/snippets/identify-server.ts`).

### Vite (React and Vue)

File: `src/main.ts`. The entry module (`src/main.ts`, or `src/main.tsx` in React), once, beside the code that mounts the app.

```ts file=esm.ts
import { Opem } from "@opem/browser";

Opem.init({ projectKey: "pk_…" });
```

- Install it first: `npm install @opem/browser`.
- The key can come from `import.meta.env.VITE_OPEM_KEY`; the key is public, so a `VITE_` variable is fine.
- In React, `OpemProvider` from `@opem/react` does the same around the app; use one, not both. The script tag before `</body>` in `index.html` works too.

### Astro

File: `src/layouts/Layout.astro`. The layout every page uses, before `</body>`.

```html
<script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" defer></script>
```

- Astro leaves a script tag with attributes other than `src` as written, so the tag loads as is, unbundled.

Signing identities on the server: the Node.js sample in the `identify` skill's signing reference (`apps/web/snippets/identify-server.ts`).

## Server-rendered

### Plain HTML

Every page, before `</body>`, or once in the footer include the pages share.

```html
<script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" defer></script>
```

- `defer` keeps it off the critical path: it runs once the page is parsed.

### Rails

File: `app/views/layouts/application.html.erb`. The application layout, before `</body>`.

```html
<script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" defer></script>
```

- To read the key from the environment, write `data-project="<%= ENV.fetch("OPEM_PUBLISHABLE_KEY") %>"`; the key is public, so it can also stay as written.

Signing identities on the server: the Ruby sample in the `identify` skill's signing reference (`apps/web/snippets/identity/sign.rb`).

### Django

File: `templates/base.html`. The base template every page extends, before `</body>`.

```html
<script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" defer></script>
```

- Keep it outside every `{% block %}`, so a child template cannot drop it.

Signing identities on the server: the Python sample in the `identify` skill's signing reference (`apps/web/snippets/identity/sign.py`).

### Laravel

File: `resources/views/layouts/app.blade.php`. The layout every view extends, before `</body>`.

```html
<script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" defer></script>
```

- Keep it outside every `@section` and `@yield`. With a component layout (`<x-layouts.app>`), the same tag goes in `resources/views/components/layouts/app.blade.php`.

Signing identities on the server: the PHP sample in the `identify` skill's signing reference (`apps/web/snippets/identity/sign.php`).

### .NET (Razor layout)

File: `Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml`. The shared layout (`Pages/Shared/_Layout.cshtml` in Razor Pages), before `</body>`, after `@await RenderSectionAsync("Scripts", required: false)`.

```html
<script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" defer></script>
```

- In a Blazor Web App the same tag goes in `Components/App.razor`, before `</body>`.

Signing identities on the server: the C# sample in the `identify` skill's signing reference (`apps/web/snippets/identity/sign.cs`).

### Java, Spring (Thymeleaf)

File: `src/main/resources/templates/layout.html`. The layout or footer fragment every page includes, before `</body>`.

```html
<script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" defer></script>
```

- Thymeleaf writes the tag out as it is; to set the key from the model, use `th:attr="data-project=${opemKey}"`.

Signing identities on the server: the Java sample in the `identify` skill's signing reference (`apps/web/snippets/identity/sign.java`).

### Go (html/template)

File: `templates/base.html`. The base template the pages share, before `</body>`.

```html
<script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" defer></script>
```

- A tag written in the template is output as written; `html/template` escapes only the values it inserts, so `data-project="{{.OpemKey}}"` works too.

Signing identities on the server: the Go sample in the `identify` skill's signing reference (`apps/web/snippets/identity/sign.go`).

## Mobile shells

### Flutter and React Native (WebView)

In the web app the WebView loads, where its own framework's entry says; nothing goes in the native code.

```html
<script src="https://support.opem.app/v1/widget.js" data-project="pk_…" defer></script>
```

- A WebView loading your web app carries the widget as the page does; there is no native SDK.
- JavaScript must be on in the WebView: `javaScriptEnabled` (the default) in react-native-webview, `JavaScriptMode.unrestricted` in Flutter's webview_flutter.
- The origin to allow is the web app's, such as `https://app.example.com`; a page loaded from the app's own files has no origin Opem can allow.

## Everywhere

Signed-in users: call `Opem.identify()` after the person signs in (the `identify` skill). Single-page apps: call `Opem.context({ page })` on each route change so requests name your routes (the `customise` skill).

Do not load the script in an iframe or through a tag manager that strips `data-project`; the widget reads the key from its own script element.
